facts.subject: opening
facts.fact: Alistair was summoned with the four heroes; Court Mage Serika Amamiya's appraisal lens went dark on him and she called it a summoning error, a fragment pulled through by accident.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: gold pouch
facts.fact: Court Mage Serika Amamiya pressed a pouch of twenty-five gold into Alistair's palm and suggested the service sector; the Guild registers anyone.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: palace wards
facts.fact: The palace wards and crystals pass over Alistair; his Living Relic Blade thrums at its side, its indignation felt only by him.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: Toma protest
facts.fact: Toma objected openly in the throne room that Alistair came through with them and is part of the count; Yui said the decision was made before the light faded.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: Suzuha asked his name
facts.fact: Princess Suzuha Sumeragi stopped the guards and asked Alistair's name, calling him 'collateral'.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: Toma's snack
facts.fact: Toma waited at the side door and gave Alistair a warm cloth-wrapped snack of bread and salted meat (eat before noon), saying the Guild registers anyone: 'That's not exile, that's a door. Doors work both ways.'
facts.evidence: Toma presses a cloth-wrapped snack into Alistair's hand

facts.subject: Suzuha's order
facts.fact: Suzuha, no warmth, ordered the guards to see that Alistair passes unharmed, then added 'If convenient' a half-second late; Court Mage Serika Amamiya declared the matter closed and ordered the misfire logged.
facts.evidence: Suzuha: 'Guards, see that he passes unharmed.' ... 'If convenient.'

facts.subject: Daigo's jab
facts.fact: Daigo jeered 'Hey, zero! At least tip the pouch on your way out!' and then went quiet; nobody laughed. Yui watched the pouch's weight and filed the number away.
facts.evidence: Daigo: brittle bravado; Yui fixes on the pouch's weight

facts.subject: Rin at the window
facts.fact: Rin watched Alistair leave from a high window, jaw set, thumb running along her sword guard.
facts.evidence: High above, through a window slit, Rin watches

facts.subject: Toma's offer
facts.fact: Toma offered Alistair one favor, one contact or one honest answer, whenever he wants it, no clock on it; Alistair said he will take him up on it one day.
facts.evidence: Toma: 'one favor, one contact, or one honest answer whenever you want it' / Alistair: 'I'll take you up on it one day'

facts.subject: Toma's warning
facts.fact: Toma warned Alistair that a grand campaign of frontier dungeons and demon-border work is coming and the Crown will spend the heroes like coin; watch who spends you. Toma said aloud at the Guild that cutting Alistair from the roster was wrong.
facts.evidence: Toma at the counter: 'watch who spends you'

facts.subject: Mizuho's first words
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku, head of the main counter at the Aureliath branch of the Adventurer's Guild, read Alistair's gear in one glance, said his sword is better cared for than he looks rested, folded a rejected application into a paper crane, and told him the form can wait until she knows what she is stamping.
facts.evidence: Mizuho's greeting at the counter

facts.subject: Toma's strap
facts.fact: Toma tightened a loose strap on Alistair's pauldron unasked ('Would've rattled loose by noon'), told him 'Eat well. Register loud', and left the Guild Hall under a plain grey cloak to return to the palace before he is missed.
facts.evidence: Toma tugs the pauldron strap, then heads out through the doors

facts.subject: Mizuho knows Toma is a hero
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku recognised Toma as a Hero of the Realm, watched the door three seconds too long, and asked Alistair for his name and what he needs (registration, contract board access, or just admiring the paperwork); she told him to choose his first job like it matters.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'first time a Hero of the Realm has done my queue-jumping for me' ... 'Choose your first job like it matters.'

facts.subject: Guild registration rules
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku explained that registration puts Alistair in the Guild's book (rank card, bank access, quest board rights); everyone starts at F-Rank; the Guild keeps no file on what the Crown discards ('what they log at the palace stays at the palace').
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'Registration puts you in our book. Rank card, bank access, quest board rights. F-Rank to start'

facts.subject: Mizuho's lesson
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku told Alistair 'Rank is just a number. Whether you come back is a habit', 'I stamp people alive, not clever', to pick something small for his first job and not die before she has learned his name; she set a folded paper crane on the counter between them like a marker on a map.
facts.evidence: Mizuho's counter lesson and the crane

facts.subject: Alistair registered
facts.fact: Alistair Zebias is a registered F-Rank adventurer with a plain iron card, no party; Mizuho corrected his form ('officially employed as loneliness') and stamped it.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'Alistair Zebias, F-Rank, no party, one very good sword.'

facts.subject: Kazuki met
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara, a first-day F-Rank like Alistair, introduced himself at the notice board, called the rat culls bad pay but safe, and said of the unstamped slip: no stamp means no escrow, and the Guild never heard of you; his 'auntie-clerk' (Mizuho) would fold a hundred cranes.
facts.evidence: Kazuki's chat at the posting wall

facts.subject: unstamped slip
facts.fact: A plain-sealed slip with no counter stamp hangs on the Guild notice board between a lost-cat job and a herb-gathering contract; nobody takes it. A runner tapped it twice before leaving.
facts.evidence: The runner taps one slip twice before leaving - a plain-sealed paper with no counter stamp

facts.subject: the dusk slip
facts.fact: Alistair took the unstamped slip off the Guild notice board on Day 1. Terms: a quiet courier errand at dusk, one delivery, no questions; gold pay above any F-Rank posting's monthly pay; 'ask for the courier in grey'; no Guild seal.
facts.evidence: He unfolds the parchment: a quiet courier errand at dusk, one delivery, no questions ... ask for the courier in grey

facts.subject: Mizuho on the slip
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku saw Alistair take the slip, called him to the counter very politely, held out her palm for it, and called it 'bait with a price tag'; she asked who posts jobs behind her counter with no stamp, no escrow and no name.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'That's not a contract. That's bait with a price tag.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's reaction
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara laughed nervously, said people take such slips all the time, 'probably', and his eyes flicked to the gold figure on the slip.
facts.evidence: Kazuki: 'It's fine! People take those all the time. Probably.'

facts.subject: Mizuho's condition
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku will not stamp the unstamped slip and will not say why, but does not forbid it ('F-Rank means you're free to make your own mistakes'). Condition: if Alistair takes it, he comes back to her counter afterward and tells her whom he meets, 'not for the Guild, for me'.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'I won't stamp it. I won't tell you why ... One condition.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's bun
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara offered Alistair half his meat bun ('You look like you skipped breakfast chasing gold') and remarked that nobody is hungry enough yet to take that slip; give it a week and the food starts sounding better.
facts.evidence: Kazuki tears his meat bun in half and holds one piece out

facts.subject: the runner
facts.fact: A runner who tapped the slip earlier lingered by the great doors watching the counter exchange, then slipped out into the square.
facts.evidence: By the great doors, the runner lingers just inside the threshold
